key_insight: A store-level reinforcement learning policy safely adapts dispatch objective weights from delayed marketplace feedback to improve batching and courier efficiency while preserving delivery quality.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how to layer offline RL onto an existing combinatorial assignment optimizer, enabling deployable policy adaptation in a large-scale three-sided logistics system.
method: Learn a discrete objective-weight multiplier at the store level instead of directly changing assignments.
Train a shared value function from centralized offline logs with decentralized execution.
Use Double Q-learning plus a conservative regularizer to limit overestimation under delayed, noisy feedback.
evidence_signal: In a production switchback experiment, the offline-trained policy increased batching and reduced courier-side time costs without degrading customer-facing delivery quality.
watch_item: Because learning depends on delayed, coupled operational signals, value estimation can still be sensitive to distribution shift and reward noise in new marketplace conditions.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
